INTRODUCTION 1. EMERITUS OF CAESAREA!

1) Biographical note. Emeritus of Caesarea is, with Petillano de Cinta, the main speaker of the Schism at the Carthage Conference of 411, one of the most eminent African schismatics and one of the most original and best-known personalities.

He was born around 350 in Caesarea of Mauritania (today Cherchel), a city to which he was always linked and in whose schools he studied Eloquence and took a liking to good language. To the profane culture acquired there he later added the knowledge of the liberal arts, theology, the Holy Books and exegesis.

Donatist Christian by birth and scion of a good Caesarian bourgeois family, he was educated since childhood in sectarian traditions as well as in the classicism of the ancient schools. He entered young, it seems, into the local schismatic clergy, whose degrees he did not earn quickly. Elected Donatist bishop of Caesarea in 385, long before the Council of Bagai (c. 394), where he played a notable role, he had a long episcopacy - more than thirty years -, since he actually governed the diocese until 411, and in 418 he still retained, with his title, episcopal pretensions?
